searchText: Will create2 address output change if we move to 32 byte addresses? The magician's post proposes "a new opcode, CREATE3, that is capable of generating 32 byte addresses." I am guessing we want to avoid semantics changes to CREATE2. Because every semantics change can break something. We can get around semantics changes by inventing some indirection/abstraction-layer/compatibility-layer which is outside of current semantics. The magician's post proposes such a solution with a translation table, but I'm not sure how this would work with CREATE2. the translation table approach would work with any old-style address Are we considering extending CREATE2 semantics to also interact with the translation table? yeah I think it should Just thinking briefly, we would have to handle table collisions somehow. I would have to think more about this. when would there be table collisions? Like, if someone does the 2**80 work to make one? Yes, precisely the motivation for longer addresses. hmm I guess in that case, the table would just keep the older value, and the second address that maps to the same compressed address would just not be able to properly interact with old-style accounts Makes sense. This disincentivizes doing the 2^80 work. But creates a pathological case that people should check for collisions before deploying. At least for a while, until all the contracts migrate over to being able to support longer addresses Yes, I was thinking about this migration. It will be a challenge in social-coordination. Will be interesting to observe. > This disincentivizes doing the 2^80 work. Oh, my mistake, not true in the case of not-yet-created counterfactual contracts. But those should migrate to CREATE3 anyway. a bit extra: but why didn't Ethereum opt into base58 for shorthand encoding of addresses? I'm not aware of any specific reasons or thought that went into the current 20-byte hex encoded format, and the subsequent backwards compatible checksum format which that evolved into
